extracted.intended_audience: manufacturers and importers of PFAS, regulated entities, state and tribal agencies, researchers, public stakeholders, and members of the public preparing comments on PFAS rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Collecting and reviewing Federal Register documents and rulemaking notices related to PFAS to inform public comments, compliance, and regulatory implementation. The page is a search-results index summarizing multiple EPA (and other agency) notices, proposed/final rules, and requests for information about PFAS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance update frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA must publish interim guidance on PFAS destruction and disposal and update the guidance at least every three years, as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The interim guidance is to be updated on a triennial basis (or sooner as appropriate). Updated guidance should build on new information about feasible and appropriate technologies and identify data gaps and uncertainties needing resolution before issuing more definitive recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feasibility and appropriateness of PFAS destruction/disposal technologies
rubrics_metrics.description: Technologies recommended for destruction or disposal of PFAS and PFAS-containing materials should be those that may be feasible and appropriate for the intended use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluations should consider technical feasibility, appropriateness for specific waste streams/materials, and identify remaining data gaps and uncertainties before making definitive recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification and resolution of data gaps and uncertainties
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA identifies key data gaps and uncertainties that must be resolved before issuing more definitive recommendations about PFAS destruction and disposal technologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rulemaking documents and guidance should explicitly note where evidence is lacking and what additional data or research would be required to strengthen recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting period start/end procedural requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory actions set explicit start and end dates for data submission periods (examples: submission period begins Jan 31, 2027, or 60 days following the effective date of a forthcoming final rule; other actions change submission periods to new dates).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule texts and notices specify effective dates and alternative end dates (e.g., different end date for small manufacturers/importers). Timetables may be modified to accommodate application readiness or further rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: TSCA PFAS reporting scope (2011–2022 manufacturers/importers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Manufacturers (including importers) of PFAS in any year between 2011–2022 must report specified data to EPA related to exposure and environmental and health effects under TSCA section 8(a)(7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting is intended to create a database on previously manufactured PFAS to inform EPA actions; modifications/exemptions to scope may be proposed to reduce burden while meeting statutory requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: De minimis concentration exemption threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of de minimis concentration thresholds for PFAS in mixtures (discussion of a 1.0% by weight hazardous cut-off vs. a proposed universal 0.1% de minimis exemption).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA may propose a universal 0.1% exemption to reduce burden of determining applicable concentrations for each reportable PFAS because PFAS are typically present at low concentrations in mixtures; thresholds affect reporting obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for adding PFAS to the Toxics Release Inventory (TRI) under NDAA
rubrics_metrics.description: PFAS subject to TRI listing under Section 7321(d)(2) include: (1) 15 PFAS described by name in the NDAA, (2) each PFAS or class of PFAS for which a method to measure levels in drinking water has been validated by the Administrator, and (3) each PFAS or class used to manufacture fluorinated polymers, as determined by the Administrator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA explains which documents and activities (e.g., validated drinking-water methods, manufacturing uses) would trigger an automatic addition to TRI and discusses how PFAS categories should be treated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Triggers for automatic addition to EPCRA section 313 list
rubrics_metrics.description: A PFAS or class of PFAS shall be added to the EPCRA section 313 list beginning January 1 of the calendar year after any one of specific triggering events (examples include finalization of a toxicity value or a covered Significant New Use Rule).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices specify enumerated trigger events (e.g., Final Toxicity Value; Significant New Use Rule; addition to existing lists) and the timing for effective listing after such events.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCRA hazardous constituent listing criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: To be listed as a hazardous constituent under RCRA, substances must have been shown in scientific studies to have toxic, carcinogenic, mutagenic, or teratogenic effects on humans or other life forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA evaluates toxicity and epidemiological studies and assessments for candidate PFAS to determine whether available data meet the Agency's RCRA listing criteria; listings affect corrective-action considerations at facilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: NPDWR numeric standards and hazard-index approach
rubrics_metrics.description: National Primary Drinking Water Regulation (NPDWR) decisions include setting Maximum Contaminant Level Goals (MCLGs) and promulgating Maximum Contaminant Levels (MCLs) for individual PFAS and mixtures (examples: MCLG of zero for PFOA and PFOS; MCLs of 4 ng/L for PFOA and PFOS; 10 ng/L for PFHxS, PFNA, and HFPO-DA; Hazard Index of 1 for specified mixtures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standards are based on best available science, consideration of dose-additive health concerns, occurrence/co-occurrence in drinking water, and feasibility (treatment/technology availability).

rubrics_metrics.name: Best available technologies (BAT) for achieving PFAS MCL compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrator identifies best technology, treatment technique, or other means available for achieving compliance with maximum contaminant levels for regulated PFAS pursuant to SDWA section 1412.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule texts include tables mapping contaminants to BATs; states and systems use these to plan compliance and technology adoption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption criteria based on knowledge/ascertainability
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed exemptions for reporting may exempt activities about which manufacturers are least likely to know or reasonably ascertain, while maintaining important reporting consistent with statutory requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When carving exemptions, EPA balances burden reduction against statutory reporting needs; justification should show why the activity is unlikely to be known by reporters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationale for changing submission periods (administrative readiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA may modify the start/end of submission periods to ensure the reporting application and collection systems are ready and to allow time to consider public comments and finalize any modifications prior to data collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delays or changes are justified by application readiness, resource constraints, and the need to implement changes informed by comments to ensure accurate and complete data collection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information collection burden estimation (PRA compliance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Information collection requests (ICRs) must estimate public reporting and recordkeeping burdens (example: TSCA Section 4 Test Orders ICR estimates an average of 137 hours per response).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ICRs are published for public comment under the Paperwork Reduction Act and should include clear burden estimates, explanation of burden components, and references to supporting materials in the docket.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data items requested for PFAS-in-seafood information
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA requests information to fill data gaps regarding PFAS in seafood, including PFAS sources in the sampling locale, relationships between environmental samples and seafood samples, and factors specific to geographic locations affecting PFAS accumulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents should supply historical information, sampling locale data, observed relationships between environmental and seafood PFAS levels, and location-specific factors to help identify patterns/trends for predicting contamination and informing mitigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of intentional vs. incidental (unintentionally present) PFAS in products
rubrics_metrics.description: GSA's Notice of Inquiry asks whether attention should be limited to intentionally added PFAS (i.e., PFAS added to serve an intended function) versus all PFAS present in products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments should explain implications of focusing only on intentionally added PFAS, including detection/identification limitations and downstream impacts; discuss alternatives and potential unintended impacts of prohibitions or reduction requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment methodology preference over registries (VA PFAS–kidney cancer assessment)
rubrics_metrics.description: VA elected not to create a PFAS registry because self-reported registries have limited scientific value; instead VA is conducting epidemiologic studies and reviewing claims data to assess links between PFAS exposure and kidney cancer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For determinations about presumptive benefits or health associations, EPA/VA emphasize epidemiologic study methods and claims-data review rather than self-reported registries; public comments are solicited to inform study design and inclusion criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information sought regarding fluorinated-container PFAS formation and uses
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA requests data on the number, location, and uses of fluorinated containers in the U.S., uses critical to national economy/security/critical infrastructure, alternatives to fluorination, and measures to mitigate PFAS generated during fluorination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responses should identify industrial uses, critical applications (including medical), existence of alternatives, and feasible mitigation strategies; this information will inform potential TSCA section 6 risk management decisions.
